records.label: Conference follow-up
records.opening: Hi Alex, it was great meeting you at the conference and hearing how your team is approaching the product launch. I'm going to ask Shannon to coordinate a conversation between your head of product and our research lead so we can compare notes on the questions we discussed. In the meantime, I wanted to follow up on a couple of points from our conversation.
records.cover:
Hi Alex, it was great meeting you at the conference and hearing how your team is approaching the product launch. I'm going to ask Shannon to coordinate a conversation between your head of product and our research lead so we can compare notes on the questions we discussed. In the meantime, I wanted to follow up on a couple of points from our conversation.

Our discussion about the launch timeline was really helpful in shaking out some of the misunderstandings I had going into the conversation with my team. I am curious to understand better how your approach differs from ours, as we've had some mixed signals from some of our key stakeholders. How do you go about prioritizing features and handling the inevitable trade-offs with respect to market release vs. platform updates? Are there any particular metrics or benchmarks that you find useful in evaluating the effectiveness of your approach? Additionally, how do you handle the handover from research to development, particularly when it comes to testing and feedback loops? I'm looking for some practical advice on how to smooth out our own transition from discovery to delivery. For example, what kind of testing have you done on your pre-launch builds, and how do you collaborate with development to test and validate your research findings? I'm hoping to learn more about your process and see if there are any best practices that we can apply to our own work.

records.label: History chapter
records.opening: Hi Morgan, thanks again for your comments on the chapter. I'm narrowing the discussion of trade and port cities so that it follows the people involved in a single journey before stepping back to the wider historical picture. I think that will give readers a clearer way into the topic, but I'd like your thoughts on how to connect that opening with the rest of the chapter.
records.cover:
Hi Morgan, thanks again for your comments on the chapter. I'm narrowing the discussion of trade and port cities so that it follows the people involved in a single journey before stepping back to the wider historical picture. I think that will give readers a clearer way into the topic, but I'd like your thoughts on how to connect that opening with the rest of the chapter.

I was thinking of breaking up the page and adding a map to map the route, perhaps a small inset image to highlight the key ports and trade stops. This would also be a good opportunity to introduce the local dialects and scripts associated with that region. 

Alternatively, I could try to weave more about the specific person or family involved in that journey into the foreground, to make it more relatable and human-scale for the reader. But that might make the chapter harder to carry on from, so I'm having a bit of a stalemate. Do either of those ideas work for you? 

Not sure how deeply to go into the local histories and economies at this point. Want us to stay in this macro view of trade and port cities, or start to drill down into the specifics of what's happening on the ground.
